title: Voz pasiva: reformas liberales del Estado

sections.content: Passive voice keeps the law or the institution as the subject through a chain of reforms — a law was enacted, marriage was converted, a registry was created, property was nationalized — exactly the shape a legal-reform narrative needs. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Entre 1855 y 1863 fueron promulgadas las llamadas Leyes de Reforma, impulsadas por Benito Juárez.
items.english: Between 1855 and 1863, the so-called Reform Laws, driven by Benito Juárez, were enacted.

items.spanish: El matrimonio fue convertido en un contrato civil independiente del sacramento religioso.
items.english: Marriage was turned into a civil contract independent of the religious sacrament.

items.spanish: Fue creado un registro civil encargado de documentar oficialmente nacimientos, matrimonios y defunciones.
items.english: A civil registry was created, tasked with officially documenting births, marriages and deaths.

items.spanish: Estas reformas fueron rechazadas con las armas por sectores conservadores, y el país fue sumido en la Guerra de Reforma.
items.english: These reforms were rejected by force by conservative sectors, and the country was plunged into the War of Reform.

sections.content: Fue convertido en / fue creado / fue sumido en all use ser + participle to mark a decisive, dated turning point — contrast this with the imperfect passive (era controlado, estaba prohibido) you'd use for a standing condition rather than a single dramatic change.
